failures.title: Reward screen: focus is never re-initialised and A/D retarget it, so an ordinary movement tap makes Enter destroy the reward silently (both full-run captures took 0 of 6 drafts)
failures.evidence:
CRITIC (docs/critiques/certification-B-r3.md, F1): isolation probe captures/certB3-focus.console.txt. Leg A (no key after room_cleared): focused = Take; Enter takes. Leg B (one fresh 60 ms KeyD tap ~200 ms after room_cleared): focused = Decline with runUi().held=[] stale=[], and the following Enter moves to path with takes unchanged, skills unchanged, freeSkillSlots unchanged - the reward is destroyed with no confirmation. Full runs certB3-b2b and certB3-b2c (Enter-first handler) finished with ZERO draft_taken across 8 rooms; certB3-b2d (ArrowLeft before Enter) took 6/6 and its focusOnArrival dumps show rn-decline rn-focus on arrival at rooms 1, 3, 4, 6.
REFUTER 1 (harness lens, reproduced, NOT an artifact) - CORRECTED MECHANISM: there is no fade-in window; the draft screen is open and opacity 1 within 10-18 ms of room_cleared. A/D are bound as the same choose-left/right as the arrows (the hint reads "A/D or <-/-> choose - Enter commit - Esc decline"), and ArrowRight produces the identical Decline focus. The held/stale gate DOES cover a key held across the clear (L4: held ["KeyD"], stale ["KeyD"], focus stays Take). THE REAL DEFECT IS BIGGER: the reward screen never re-initialises its focus - at L3-a a freshly opened room-3 draft, 3162 ms after its clear, with ZERO keys pressed in that leg, arrived already on rn-decline rn-focus, inherited from a KeyD two screens earlier. One D anywhere arms Decline on every later reward screen until the player presses left. Focus does not track card type or slot availability (L4 NODE draft with freeSkillSlots 0 still defaulted to Take).
REFUTER 2 (bar lens): outcome reproduces exactly; ruled it the documented control of the screen rather than a REFERENCE_BAR clause violation. ORCHESTRATOR RULING: blocking anyway - a "fully playable" loop cannot silently destroy the run reward under an ordinary strafing pattern; a Decline-focused screen contradicts the rn-primary Take it tells the player to commit.
REQUIRED FIX (all three): (1) every reward/draft/path screen re-initialises focus to its rn-primary (Take) on open, never inheriting focus from a previous screen; (2) choose-left/right input (A, D, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight) is ignored for a grace window of ~300 ms after a screen opens AND any key that is down at open must be released before it counts (extend the held/stale gate to fresh taps inside the grace window); (3) Decline must never be the focused button unless the player deliberately moved there after the grace window - and Esc remains the decline path. Keep the documented A/D choose binding after the grace window. Verify with the critic probe (legs A-D) AND a full 8-room real-input run that takes 6/6 drafts with the strafing pattern of certB3-b2b.
failures.reproduce: cd echoes-three && node tools/cert-capture.mjs shot certfixB4-focus --url "http://127.0.0.1:5199/?seed=777" --settle 4000 --actions tools/actions/certB3-focus.json --timeout 180000 ; compare the [EVAL] lines A-no-key-pressed (focused Take) vs B-one-KeyD-tap (focused Decline) vs B-afterEnter (screen path, takes unchanged). Also tools/actions/certB3-ref1-focus.json (legs L1-L4, incl. L3-a inherited-focus proof) and the full-run file tools/actions/certB3-b2b.json (must end with 6/6 drafts taken).
